newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia threatens punishment over Timor protest.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia threatens punishment over Timor protest.

text.p: Indonesian police have threatened heavy punishment for three East Timorese protestors over an anti-integration demonstration in the territory's capital Dili this week, the Antara news agency reported on Friday.

"The thing they did was an action that spread hatred against the head of state, so they can receive a heavy punishment of 20 years in jail," East Timor police chief Colonel Jusuf Mucharam was quoted as saying.
"However, with the evidence and confessions we have for the time being they can be jailed for 15 years," he said.
The protest by about 500 youths occurred outside the headquarters of the Dili Catholic diocese after Nobel Peace Prize winner Bishop Carlos Belo gave a news conference.

Those arrested are believed to have been protestors carrying a banner with anti-integration slogans as well as picture depicting Indonesian President Suharto holding two bloody skulls and with a bloodied bone in his mouth.
One of the banners' captions read: "Suharto eats East Timorese bones".
Mucharam said so far only the three teenagers had been detained for their part in the protest and police were still looking for the masterminds behind it.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in December 1975 and declared the former Portuguese colony its 27th province in July the following year in an act not recognised by the United Nations.
